report: Technique: MRI of the right knee. Results: Test report. Minimal effusion. Medial meniscus tear. Lateral meniscus normal.  Chondromalacia medial, lateral and patelofemoral compartment. No baker's cyst. Impression: Medial meniscus tear. Chondromalacia of all three compartments.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 58-year-old male with right knee pain. Evaluate ACL. Partial knee replacement.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or contusion. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: High-grade partial tear at the posterior root attachment, with moderate extrusion of the body.
Medial compartment cartilage: Severe chondrosis with full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial femoral condyle and tibial plateau with subchondral edema. Marginal osteophytes.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Moderate chondrosis with low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss in the lateral femoral condyle and full-thickness cartilage loss in the central lateral tibial plateau. Marginal osteophytes.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Moderate chondrosis, with diffuse cartilage thinning and areas of full-thickness cartilage fissuring in the patella and femoral trochlea. Marginal osteophyte.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Mucoid degeneration of the ACL.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Lateral patellar tilt and translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Increased tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 22 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Progress tricompartmental moderate osteoarthritis, with severe chondrosis in the medial compartment.
2.	High-grade tear of the posterior root attachment of the medial meniscus, with extrusion of the body.
3.	New mucoid degeneration of the ACL.

MRI of left Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc LT, Sag PD FS, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, Ax T2 FS, Screen Save



Osteophytes and irregular thining of intra-articular cartilage of left knee, reflecting osteoarthritis; grade 4 chondromalacia of patella and medial femoral trochlea
Subchondral bone marrow edema/cysts of knee
Focal lobulated hyperintensity foci in tibial plateua on F/ST2WI, R/O intraosseous ganglion cyst cysts.
Patellar enthesophyte and tendinosis of quadriceps tendon.
Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of  grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration or meniscal vascularity 
> No strong MR evidence of tear of lateral meniscus.
> Mild subarticular edema over tibial spine.
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Subcutaneous edema over left knee.
> A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst.
> Increased fat stranding and minimal fluid accumulation located along the pes anserinus, R/O Anserine bursitis

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee, more severe at patellofemoral joint.
2. Mild synovitis of left knee and Baker's cyst.
3. Mild Anserine bursitis.
4. R/O intraosseous ganglion cyst in tibial plateua.
5. Subcutaneous edema over left knee.
6. Grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration 
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

SOL DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Lateral menisküs anterior hornunda radial yırtık izlendi. Medial menisküste volüm kaybı ,grade III dejenerasyon, kök ve kompleks yırtık ile uyumlu görünüm mevcuttur. Menisküs 5 mm ekstrüde görünümde .Arka çapraz bağ, lateral ve medial kollateral ligaman normaldir. Anterior çapraz bağda mukoid dejenerasyon ile uyumlu sinyal artışı mevcuttur.Distal kuadriseps ve patellar tendonlar normaldir. Retinaküler devamsızlık yoktur.Diz ekleminde  hafif sıvı artışı izlendiGastroknemius medial krurus bacağında tendonda tendinozis ile uyumlu sinyal artışı mevcuttur.Diz eklemini oluşturan tibia ve femoral kemik yapılarda marginal ve santral osteofitik sivrileşmeler özellikle medial eklem aralığında azalma ve medial eklem düzeyinde tibial kartilajda belirgin incelme mevcuttur (dejeneratif artrit bulguları ). Ayrıca tibia interkondiler tüberkül düzeyinde subkondral kemik iliği ödemi ve yine femur interkondiler düzeyinde subkondral milimetrik kistler izlenmiştir.

Aus der Vordiagnostik [DATE] bek. und hierzu progrediente, medial betonte Pangonarthrose mit flächig vollschichtiger Chondropathie beider Gelenkpartner in der Belastungszone mit Ausdünnung und teils Mehrsklerosierierung der subchondralen Kortikalis sowie progredienter ausgedehnter subchondraler Reizreaktion femorotibial. Oberflächliche Chondropathie auch in den anderen Gelenkkompartimenten ohne tiefergreifende Läsion. Außenmeniskus gering mukoid ohne Riss. Innenmeniskus bei mukoider Vorschädigung mit Lappenriss in der Pars intermedia und umgeschlagenen Anteil auf die Meniskussubstanz parafemoral (5/20). Medial ausgeprägte Reizzustand des Kapselbandapparates. VKB gering mukoid. Ansonsten Bandapparat regelrecht. Kleine Plica mediopatellaris. Geringer Gelenkerguss, dtl. chron. Reizsynovialitis, minimal flüssigkeitsgefüllte Baker-Zyste.
